audit_findings.title: Environmental claims could materially exceed recorded reserves
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional remediation payments would reduce future owner earnings or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The actual cost could be materially higher as there has not been a determination of how those costs will be allocated among the PRPs at the sites.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated valuation error. The latest filing records $10.0 million of total environmental reserves, including $3.8 million for Portland Harbor and Newark Bay, while the Portland Harbor remedy was estimated at $1.1 billion present value and $1.7 billion undiscounted across more than 80 parties. Koppers claims de minimis status, but allocation remains unresolved, so its incremental share and materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the private allocation expected by the end of 2026, related settlement proposals, Koppers-specific probability ranges and payment timing; rerun the valuation for any liability exceeding the recorded reserve.

audit_findings.title: Material asset-retirement obligations may be entirely unrecorded
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecorded legally required closure and remediation cash flows would reduce future owner earnings or enter the equity bridge as an additional liability.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain conditional asset retirement obligations related to facilities have not been recorded in the consolidated financial statements due to uncertainties surrounding the ultimate settlement date and estimate of fair value related to a legal obligation to perform an asset retirement activity.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility. The filing confirms that some conditional legal obligations remain unrecorded because settlement dates and fair values cannot be estimated and states that eventual recognition may be material. The June 2026 recognition of an $18.5 million short-term Stickney asset-retirement obligation addresses part of the exposure but does not quantify the remaining unrecorded facility obligations.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a site-by-site inventory of unrecorded obligations, including triggering events, expected settlement dates and probability-weighted closure, residue-removal, demolition and remediation costs; rerun OE and the bridge once estimable.

audit_findings.title: Reliance on Beazer indemnification masks potentially large liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: Indemnitor default, disputed coverage or excluded claims would shift legal and environmental cash payments into owner earnings or create a liability deduction in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If for any reason (including disputed coverage or financial incapability) one or more of such parties fail to perform their obligations and we are held liable for or otherwise required to pay all or part of such liabilities without reimbursement, the imposition of such liabilities on us could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking counterparty and coverage risk, not a demonstrated present omission: the filing says Beazer and other indemnitors have performed their obligations in all material respects to date. Because qualified expenditures have no monetary limit and the gross covered liabilities are not disclosed, a future failure could be material but cannot presently be measured.
audit_findings.action: Monitor Beazer East and guarantor creditworthiness, arbitration or coverage disputes, post-2019 tenders and claims outside the indemnity; rerun only if performance deteriorates or a Koppers-retained amount becomes probable and estimable.

audit_findings.title: Known shutdown cash costs may be missing from projected owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $68.6 million to $82.6 million of expected shutdown cash charges remaining after June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The remaining one-time shutdown payments should be deducted from forecast owner earnings or separately from operating value, with associated changes to post-shutdown earnings and maintenance capital reflected in the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect this action to result in pre-tax charges to earnings of $ 50 million to $ 54 million through the end of 2026, approximately $ 28 million of which constitutes non-cash charges and approximately $ 22 million to $ 26 million of which constitutes cash expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling omission if the forecast contains no explicit closure deduction. The latest filing estimates $79 million to $93 million of combined Stickney and phthalic-an­hydride shutdown cash charges; only $10.4 million is shown as paid through June 30, 2026, leaving approximately $68.6 million to $82.6 million before tax and discounting. That equals about 19.6% to 23.6% of the $350 million base equity value and is more than three times the $22 million OE anchor at the low end, so it is reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash paid after June 30, the $42.8 million recorded shutdown liabilities, remaining unaccrued expenditures and payment timing; rerun all scenarios with tax-affected closure cash flows plus post-wind-down contribution and maintenance-capex changes.

audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings may mix parent and consolidated claims
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent attribution of net income, depreciation, working capital, capital expenditure and cash can distort annual OE, the log-trend anchor and per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: KCCC is owned 60 percent by a wholly owned subsidiary of Koppers and 40 percent by TISCO.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved accounting-perimeter possibility rather than a demonstrated quantified error. KCCC was 40% minority-owned, and in 2024 the filed $3.8 million noncontrolling-interest loss was about 7.3% of the $52.4 million income attributable to Koppers. The direction can vary by year because minority losses, non-cash add-backs, working-capital movements and liquidation cash flows need not move together. The record does not quantify the resulting change to the $22 million trend anchor.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year on a consistently parent-common basis, allocate all consolidated cash-flow components and cash attributable to noncontrolling interests, and recompute the log trend and every valuation scenario.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat restricted operating cash as surplus common-equity cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $40.7 million, equal to $1.89 per share and 11.6% of the $350 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash that is trapped, pledged, operationally required or committed should be excluded from the cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The terms of Koppers Inc.’s Credit Facility (as defined in Note 15 - Debt) prohibit Koppers Inc. from paying dividends and otherwise transferring assets except for certain limited dividends.
audit_findings.explanation: Accessibility and surplus status remain unresolved, but the valuation effect is capped by the entire $40.7 million balance. Removing all cash would reduce every scenario by $1.89 per share; even that worst case cannot reverse the conclusion because the reported $14.01 to $17.88 value range is already far below the $47.78 market price. The filing also permits qualifying dividends and repurchases, and $43.9 million of shares were repurchased during the first half of 2026, so the evidence does not establish that all cash is legally trapped.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash by legal entity and jurisdiction, covenant eligibility, minimum operating cash and committed closure funding; classify only demonstrably surplus and accessible cash in the next bridge rerun.
